newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Products Outlook - No fireworks for gasoline.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Products Outlook - No fireworks for gasoline.

text.p: Surging gasoline demand at the pump over the coming U.S. Independence Day holiday will do little to raise spot gasoline prices, since high refinery run rates are drenching markets with product, traders said Monday.

But the same "Fourth of July" weekend is already sapping activity in cash refined oil products markets, and between now and the time NYMEX closes on Thursday for the long weekend, not much is expected, traders said.

Indeed, the only piece of potentially important news, that independent refiner Tosco was planning to pull crude units off-line at its Bayway refinery in New Jersey for three weeks of maintenance starting in July, did little to excite a market many say is oversupplied.
"My guess is that by Wednesday afternoon most people will be gone, especially with the Merc closing early," said one trader.
U.S. GULF
Conventional gasoline prices showed no sign of rebounding in the near term, according to traders, and probably will not as long as refineries keep output at such high levels.
According to the American Petroleum Institute's (API) latest report, the U.S. refining industry is running at virtually full hilt at 97.6 percent of capacity.
API also said U.S. gasoline output sat at 8.25 million barrels a day, up more than 300,000 barrels from the year-ago figure.
Gasoline prices in the USG have declined steadily for most of 1997, with the few bullish moves limited only to short-term events.
Conventional regular M-grade unleaded gasoline slipped to 52.13 cents a gallon last week, the lowest price since February 1996. Prices had peaked at 73.38 cents in October before trending lower.
Market traders said despite the July 4 holiday, often seen as a peak in U.S. gasoline demand, no increase in buying activity in the Gulf was expected.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Traders were predicting a quiet week but views were mixed whether gasoline differentials will rise or fall as the long July fourth weekend approaches.
"It looks like a boring expiration of the July (NYMEX) contract," said a Harbor trader, referring to the expiry of both gasoline and heating oil contracts for July delivery.
"I think it will have no effect on gasoline because people look pretty well supplied," the trader said, noting steady to maybe weaker differentials.
Another gasoline player, however, said differentials could firm due to some quick short covering Tuesday and Wednesday by players trying to get an early start on the weekend.
"There could be activity to get things cleared up by Wednesday," said a trader, expecting a quarter cent gain this week on premium unleaded differentials.
On the distillates, differentials on 54-grade jet fuel fuel and 55-grade low sulphur kerosene are expected to continue creeping up after gaining about a penny last week.
"Buyers are creeping in to store barrels and to fill their tanks," said a distillate trader.
MIDCONTINENT
Midcontinent traders said they had bearish expectations for gasoline this week despite the approach of the long Fourth of July weekend.

"There's so much gasoline out there and it will probably be under even more pressure because the arbitrage is open from the (U.S.) Gulf Coast to the Midwest," one Chicago trader said, noting Chicago conventional unleaded was priced a full 3.5 cents higher than Chicago material.
Gulf material for shipment in early July was offered for 3.0 cents below August futures at midday Monday, while Chicago unleaded was pegged at a half cent over the August print.
"That more than compensates for the cost of shipping it north on the Explorer Pipeline from the Gulf," the trader said, predicting the oversupplied Midwest would therefore attract even more barrels.
Another Chicago trader also threw water on the notion that holiday driving demand would bolster gasoline differentials.
"I wouldn't fall for that line of thinking because there's too much gasoline," he said, predicting softer gasoline prices will also drag distillate values lower in the coming week.
-- New York Oil Desk 1 212 859 1633
